registros.titulo: STARLI / RESEARCH FAMILY III / FLAGSHIPS 281–285 Ten Research Flagships · Letters to Future Laboratories Five research architectures for calibration succession, automated discovery, collaboration, self-repair and quantum sensor recovery. F281 | NANO-QUANTUM RESEARCH SYSTEM CROSS-GENERATION CALIBRATION AT THE LIMIT Three-coupling: long-horizon scientific memory × traceable calibration and reference transfer × intergenerational evidence transfer. The primary proposal tests measurement unit definition survival under a concealed challenge: swap a noncommutable reference standard. Measures: reference-transfer bias [nT]; separate witness: uncertainty coverage [fraction]. Strong comparator: independent reference magnetometry with fixed calibration transfer. Failures remain reportable. F282 | INTELLIGENT MICROROBOTIC AUTOMATED SCIENTIFIC DISCOVERY AT THE LIMIT Three-coupling: long-horizon scientific memory × modular autonomous infrastructure × uncertainty-aware bounded decision. The primary proposal tests sequential experiment acquisition bias under a concealed challenge: change a microgripper contact force. Measures: held-out experiment information gain [bits]; separate witness: hypothesis replication success [fraction]. Strong comparator: randomized factorial design and classical active learning under matched budgets. Failures remain reportable. F283 | NANO-QUANTUM RESEARCH AGENT COLLABORATION AT THE LIMIT Three-coupling: long-horizon scientific memory × modular autonomous infrastructure × intergenerational evidence transfer. The primary proposal tests conflicting measurement ontology negotiation under a concealed challenge: corrupt one agent clock.
